The course is a very basic and a must-take for EE students as all the topics are fundamental. I believe the syllabus is sufficient to teach students these basics in electrical engineering. However, I think the course is not effective in the practical areas, especially in the lab works. All of the lab assignments were ahead of the topics covered in the lectures so far. Most labs were very harsh in work-load and the expectations were too high. I believe this prevents the students from understanding the lab topics, as we were mostly focused on managing to obtain a very low error and get a check in the lab rather than learning the concept. I think the lab assignments should be revised so that they become correlated to the covered lecture topics and the workload should be decreased, allowing more freedom to the students so that we don't have to worry about getting a check and try to practice the lecture topics more easily. I also think the pre-lab quiz is very ineffective as we are asked the same things as the preliminary lab report. These pre-lab quizzes just waste around 30 minutes of our time in the lab hours, doing the same things we did in the preliminary lab. Finally, I think the questions in the midterms/final could be digitally drawn rather than hand-drawn so we can understand the circuit more easily.
